# The script for the player isn't very important for this example.
# Just glide left and right across the bottom of the screen.
self.go_to_xy(-220, -150)
while True:
    self.glide_to_xy(220, -150, 2)
    self.glide_to_xy(-220, -150, 2)

# Make sure that only the original (hidden) Bullet responds to the
# keypress.  Without this, every clone makes a new clone and we soon
# have thousands of clones.
if self is not Bullet.the_original():
    return

# If there are already the maximum number of Bullet clones being
# fired, stop here.
if len(Bullet.all_clones()) == Bullet.max_being_fired:
    return

# Make the new Bullet clone; the "when I start as a clone" script
# below does the rest of the work.
self.create_clone()

# This variable doesn't change, but it's helpful to have a named value
# for the maximum number of Bullet clones we want to be allowed to
# exist at one time.
Bullet.max_being_fired = 10

self.hide()

# Find the player sprite ...
player = Player.the_original()
# ... and move ourselves to its location, except a bit higher ("+20"
# for the Y coordinate) so the bullet appears at the top of the ship.
self.go_to_xy(player.x_position, player.y_position + 20)

# Become visible.
self.show()

# Move quite quickly up the screen, until we're well off the top.
while self.y_position < 200:
    self.change_y(5)

# This clone has finished its job, so delete it to avoid cluttering up
# the game with lots of clones.
self.delete_this_clone()
